name: writing (Mesopotamia)
making_significance: First known writing: proto-cuneiform tablets from Uruk record goods, rations and labour.
free_sources: Met Open Access (CC0); Wikimedia Commons; open-access excavation reports
notes: Claim: earliest with Egypt, within about a century; competing: Egypt (Abydos U-j, medium). Roots in clay tokens proposed (Schmandt-Besserat, debated).

name: writing (Egypt)
making_significance: First known Egyptian writing: bone and ivory labels from tomb U-j at Abydos with signs read by some as phonetic.
materials_techniques: bone and ivory labels; ink on pots
notes: Contested: independent invention vs stimulus diffusion from Mesopotamia; U-j readings (Dreyer) debated (confidence medium).

name: writing (China)
making_significance: First known Chinese writing: a fully developed script on Shang oracle bones and bronzes at Anyang.
notes: Earlier Neolithic signs (Jiahu, Dawenkou) are not accepted as writing by most (low); script maturity implies an undocumented earlier stage.

name: writing (Mesoamerica)
other_names: Olmec, Zapotec, Epi-Olmec and Maya scripts
date_note: Cascajal Block c. 900 BCE (contested); Zapotec c. 600–400 BCE; Maya c. 300 BCE (San Bartolo)
making_significance: First known writing of the Americas, invented independently in Mesoamerica.
object_types: Cascajal Block; San José Mogote Monument 3; San Bartolo texts
notes: Cascajal Block (low: context and date questioned); Monument 3 date debated (medium); San Bartolo c. 300 BCE (high).

name: khipu as a recording system
date_note: Wari khipus c. 600–1000 CE (secure); Caral c. 2500 BCE claim (low)
making_significance: A debated case: knotted cords as an independent recording system that may or may not encode language.
notes: Caral "khipu" announced by Ruth Shady is not securely published (low); whether khipu is writing is open.

name: Indus script
date_note: Mature c. 2600–1900 BCE; early signs c. 3300 BCE at Harappa
making_significance: First known sign system of South Asia, on seals, tablets and pots; undeciphered.
notes: Whether it writes language is disputed (Farmer, Sproat and Witzel 2004 said no; most disagree).

name: alphabet
making_significance: First known alphabet: signs adapted from Egyptian hieroglyphs by Semitic-speaking workers.
object_types: Wadi el-Hol inscriptions; Serabit el-Khadim inscriptions
notes: Date range 1900–1500 BCE debated; made by workers and miners, not scribes (F1.23).

name: rongorongo
date_note: Tablet D (Échancrée) is on wood felled c. 1493–1509 CE (Ferrara et al. 2024); tablets O, Q and three Rome tablets are on 18th–19th-century wood
making_significance: A possible independent invention of writing on Rapa Nui; undeciphered.
notes: Invention before or after European contact (Roggeveen 1722; Spanish visit 1770) is debated; old wood could be driftwood kept for years before carving.

name: zero as numeral
date_note: Long Count zero by 36 BCE (Chiapa de Corzo Stela 2); Babylonian placeholder c. 300 BCE; Indian zero (Gwalior) 876 CE
making_significance: Zero was invented more than once, as placeholder and as number.
object_types: Long Count stelae; Gwalior inscription; Bakhshali manuscript
notes: Bakhshali manuscript radiocarbon spread (3rd–10th c.) disputed.

name: counting tokens
making_significance: First known clay tokens used for counting goods; a proposed ancestor of writing.
notes: Token-to-writing thesis (Schmandt-Besserat) contested.

name: tally marks
date_note: Lebombo c. 44,000–43,000 BP; Ishango c. 20,000 BP
making_significance: Among the earliest proposed counting records: notched bones from southern and central Africa.
notes: Interpretations as calendars or arithmetic contested.

name: map (earliest known)
date_note: Babylonian Map of the World c. 600 BCE; Nippur city plan c. 1500 BCE; Mawangdui maps 168 BCE
making_significance: First known surviving world map, on a clay tablet; China's earliest topographic maps on silk follow.
object_types: Imago Mundi tablet; Nippur plan; Mawangdui maps
notes: Older "maps" (Pavlov, Çatalhöyük mural) are contested (low).

name: portolan chart
making_significance: First known surviving sea chart with rhumb lines.
notes: Date debated (late 13th century).

name: astrolabe
date_note: Oldest surviving by Nastulus 927–8; theory Hellenistic
making_significance: Earliest known surviving astrolabe, made in the Abbasid world from Greek theory.
notes: Hellenistic invention likely (Hipparchus/Ptolemy); no earlier survivals.

name: water clock
date_note: Karnak clepsydra, reign of Amenhotep III c. 1400 BCE
making_significance: First known surviving water clock.
notes: Babylonian water clocks may be as old.

name: sundial
making_significance: First known shadow clocks.

name: mechanical clock (escapement)
date_note: Su Song 1088; Yi Xing's water-driven escapement 725
making_significance: First known astronomical clock tower with an escapement, water-driven.
notes: European weight-driven verge clocks c. 1270–1300 are a separate invention (see next row).

name: mechanical clock (weight-driven)
making_significance: First known weight-driven mechanical clocks with verge escapement.
notes: Exact first date unknown; textual evidence c. 1270s–1280s.

name: geared computing device
date_note: c. 150–100 BCE (dates debated to c. 200 BCE)
making_significance: First known geared calculator, modelling the heavens.

name: pottery (South China)
making_significance: First known pottery vessels, made by hunter-gatherers long before farming.
notes: Wu et al. 2012; Yuchanyan c. 18,000 BP.

name: pottery (Japan and Amur)
date_note: Odai Yamamoto I c. 16,500 cal BP (debated); Amur c. 16,000–15,000 BP
making_significance: Early hunter-gatherer pottery in Japan and the Russian Far East, possibly independent of South China.
free_sources: ColBase (Japan Government Standard Terms); Wikimedia Commons; open-access excavation reports
notes: Relation to China debated.

name: pottery (Sahara)
making_significance: First known pottery in Africa, made by hunter-gatherers in the green Sahara; independent invention.
notes: Huysecom et al. 2009.

name: pottery (Amazonia)
date_note: c. 7,000–6,000 BP (Taperinha); San Jacinto (Colombia) and Valdivia (Ecuador) c. 4th millennium BCE
making_significance: Among the earliest pottery in the Americas, made by fisher-foragers of the lower Amazon.
notes: Dates (Roosevelt 1991) debated.

name: pottery (Southwest Asia)
making_significance: Pottery arrives after farming in Southwest Asia, reversing the East Asian order.
notes: Teaches that the "Neolithic package" is regional.

name: fired clay figurines
making_significance: First known fired-clay objects, made before any pottery vessel.

name: glass
date_note: Glass beads c. 2500 BCE (Mesopotamia); core-formed vessels c. 1500 BCE
making_significance: First known true glass, as beads, then vessels.
notes: Faience and glazes older.

name: glassblowing
making_significance: First known blown glass, which made glass cheap and common.
object_types: Jewish Quarter (Jerusalem) waste; Roman blown glass

name: primary glass in West Africa
making_significance: First known glass made from raw materials in sub-Saharan Africa, a distinct high-lime high-alumina glass.
notes: Babalola et al. 2017–2018.

name: synthetic pigment
making_significance: First known synthetic pigment, a calcium copper silicate.

name: lacquer
date_note: Kuahuqiao lacquered bow c. 8,000 BP; Kakinoshima B (Hokkaido) lacquered threads from a burial dated c. 9,000 cal BP on soil samples, contested; burial context suggests c. 8,000–7,000 BP
making_significance: First known lacquer use, recorded on a bow in China; a competing Japanese claim is older but contested.
notes: Kakinoshima dating challenged (low); Kuahuqiao medium.

name: porcelain
date_note: Sui–Tang white porcelain c. 6th–7th century; Eastern Han proto-porcelain
making_significance: First known true porcelain, high-fired white ware from northern China.
free_sources: Met Open Access (CC0); National Palace Museum Taipei Open Data; Wikimedia Commons
notes: Definition of "porcelain" varies; some date it to the Eastern Han.

name: hard-paste porcelain (Europe)
making_significance: European reinvention of hard-paste porcelain after centuries of imports.
free_sources: Met Open Access (CC0); Rijksmuseum (CC0); Wikimedia Commons
notes: A recurrence by imitation, not independent (F1.14).

name: rubber processing
date_note: Rubber balls at El Manatí c. 1600 BCE; processing described by Hosler et al. 1999
making_significance: First known processed rubber: latex mixed with morning-glory juice to make bouncing balls, sandals and bands.
notes: Goodyear's vulcanisation (1844) is a later recurrence.

name: vulcanised rubber
making_significance: Industrial recurrence of stabilised rubber by heating with sulphur.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)
notes: Goodyear/Hancock priority dispute.

name: plastic (semi-synthetic and synthetic)
making_significance: First known plastics, moulded from cellulose and later from phenol-formaldehyde.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)

name: paper
date_note: Western Han fragments (e.g. Fangmatan) 2nd century BCE; Cai Lun credited 105 CE
making_significance: First known paper, made from plant fibre pulp.
notes: The Cai Lun story is a tradition; archaeology shows earlier paper (F1.3).

name: paper outside China
date_note: Baghdad mill c. 794; Samarkand earlier by tradition
making_significance: First known paper production outside China, in the Abbasid world.
free_sources: Qatar Digital Library (open licence); Wikimedia Commons
notes: The Talas (751) prisoners story is a legend.

name: bark paper
date_note: Beaters from the early 1st millennium CE or earlier
making_significance: An independent bark-paper tradition in Mesoamerica, beaten rather than pulped.
notes: Not "paper" in the Chinese pulp sense; beater dating uncertain.

name: woodblock printing (dated)
date_note: Diamond Sutra 868 (earliest dated printed book); Bulguksa dharani before 751 (undated); Hyakumantō Darani 764–770
making_significance: First known dated printed book, and earlier undated prints in Korea and Japan.
object_types: Diamond Sutra; Mugujeonggwang dharani; Hyakumantō Darani
notes: Korean dharani dating debated (before 751).

name: block printing in the Islamic world
making_significance: First known printing in the Islamic world: block-printed amulets.

name: movable type (ceramic)
making_significance: First known movable type, of fired clay.
notes: No surviving books from Bi Sheng.

name: movable metal type
date_note: Jikji 1377 (earliest extant); earlier metal-type books recorded c. 1230s
making_significance: Earliest surviving book printed with movable metal type.
defined_by: historians; UNESCO Memory of the World
notes: Jikji is in Paris (BnF); return requested by Korea.

name: printing press
making_significance: First known printing press with cast movable type and oil ink in Europe.
materials_techniques: screw press; type metal; oil ink
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Library of Congress (PD items)
notes: A recurrence; no proven transfer from East Asia.

name: lithography
making_significance: First planographic printing, from limestone.

name: photography (Niépce)
making_significance: First known surviving camera photograph.
object_types: View from the Window at Le Gras
notes: Daguerre (1839) and Talbot (1839–41) made practical processes.

name: photography (Hércules Florence)
making_significance: An independent invention of photographic printing in Brazil, named "photographie" by its maker.
notes: Recognised by B. Kossoy (1970s); a case of who gets written in (F1.3).

name: electric telegraph
date_note: Cooke and Wheatstone 1837; Morse 1837–1844; Chappe optical 1794
making_significance: First practical electric telegraphs.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)
notes: Multiple claimants.

name: sound recording
date_note: Scott de Martinville phonautograph 1857; Edison phonograph 1877 (playback)
making_significance: First known recording of sound, then playback.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Library of Congress (PD items)

name: motion picture
making_significance: First known moving-picture films and public screenings.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Library of Congress (PD items)
notes: Contested firsts by definition.

name: programmable computer
date_note: Zuse Z3 1941; Colossus 1943–44; ENIAC 1945; Babbage's Analytical Engine designed 1837
making_significance: First working programmable computers.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)
notes: "First" depends on definition; women programmers of ENIAC obscured (F1.23).

name: World Wide Web
making_significance: First hypertext system on the internet, by Tim Berners-Lee at CERN.

name: video game
making_significance: First known interactive video games.
notes: Earlier claims (1947 cathode-ray amusement device) exist.

name: farming (Fertile Crescent)
date_note: Cultivation c. 9500 BCE; domestic forms c. 8500 BCE
making_significance: First known domestication of wheat, barley, lentil and pea.
notes: Multi-centre protracted model vs core area.

name: farming (China)
date_note: Millet c. 8000–6000 BCE (north); rice domestication c. 7000–5000 BCE (Yangtze)
making_significance: Independent domestication of rice and millets.
notes: Shangshan rice use c. 9000 BCE claimed.

name: farming (New Guinea)
making_significance: Independent agriculture of taro, banana and yam with drainage ditches.
notes: Kuk is a World Heritage site; counters the idea that farming came from outside.

name: farming (Mesoamerica)
date_note: Squash c. 8000 BCE (Guilá Naquitz); maize c. 7000 BCE (Balsas, Xihuatoxtla)
making_significance: Independent domestication of squash, then maize from teosinte.

name: farming (Andes and Amazonia)
date_note: Squash c. 8000 BCE (Ñanchoc); manioc c. 8000 BCE; potato c. 6000 BCE
making_significance: Independent domestication of potato, quinoa, manioc, squash, peanut and cotton.

name: farming (Eastern North America)
making_significance: Independent domestication of squash, sunflower, sumpweed and goosefoot.

name: farming (Sahel and West Africa)
date_note: Pearl millet c. 2500 BCE (Mali); sorghum c. 3000 BCE (eastern Sudan)
making_significance: Independent domestication of pearl millet, sorghum, African rice and yams.

name: farming (Ethiopian highlands)
making_significance: Domestication of teff, enset and noog in the Ethiopian highlands.
notes: Poor archaeobotanical record.

name: farming (South Asia)
making_significance: Early farming with barley and locally domesticated zebu cattle.

name: aquaculture
date_note: Oldest dated channel c. 6,600 years ago
making_significance: Among the earliest known aquaculture: Gunditjmara channels and weirs for kooyang.
notes: Dating reported for one channel; ancient Chinese carp culture is a later recurrence.

name: bread
making_significance: First known bread, baked by hunter-gatherers before farming.
notes: Arranz-Otaegui et al. 2018.

name: beer and fermented drink
date_note: Raqefet Cave c. 13,000 BP (contested); Jiahu mixed drink c. 7000 BCE
making_significance: First known fermented drinks, from the Natufian Levant and Neolithic China.
notes: Raqefet claim debated (low); Jiahu residue study (McGovern 2004, medium).

name: wine
making_significance: First known grape wine, in jars in southern Georgia.
notes: McGovern et al. 2017; links to qvevri practice.

name: cheese
making_significance: First known cheese-making, from milk residues in perforated pots.
notes: Salque et al. 2013.

name: cacao use
making_significance: First known cacao use, in the upper Amazon rather than Mesoamerica.
notes: Zarrillo et al. 2018 revised the Mesoamerican-first view.

name: coffee drinking
date_note: Mid-15th century Sufi circles in Yemen
making_significance: First credible evidence of coffee as a drink.
notes: Ethiopian goatherd legend is later folklore.

name: nixtamalisation
making_significance: Treating maize with lime, which made it nutritionally complete; a Mesoamerican invention.
notes: Earliest evidence poorly dated.

name: dog domestication
date_note: Bonn-Oberkassel c. 14,200 BP; earlier claims contested
making_significance: First domesticated animal, from wolves, among hunter-gatherers.
notes: Place (Europe, Siberia, East Asia) debated.

name: horse domestication at Botai (revised)
making_significance: A changed first: Botai horses were long taught as the first domesticated or ridden horses; genomics (2018) show they are ancestors of Przewalski's horses, not of modern domestic horses.
notes: Outram et al. 2009 (bit wear, milk) vs Gaunitz et al. 2018; Botai herding still argued.

name: horse domestication (DOM2)
making_significance: First known ancestors of modern domestic horses, spreading fast with spoked-wheel chariots.
notes: Librado et al. 2021; Yamnaya riding claim (Trautmann et al. 2023) contested.

name: dromedary domestication
making_significance: First domesticated dromedaries in Arabia, which opened desert caravan trade.
notes: Dates debated; UAE sites (e.g. Tell Abraq, Mleiha) relevant.

name: llama and alpaca domestication
making_significance: Domestication of camelids in the Andes for fibre, meat and carrying.

name: native copper working
date_note: Çayönü c. 8200 BCE; Shanidar pendant c. 8700 BCE (approximate)
making_significance: First known metal working: cold-hammered and annealed native copper.

name: copper smelting (Balkans)
making_significance: First known copper smelting from ore.
notes: Radivojević et al. 2010; competes with Iran.

name: copper smelting (Iran)
making_significance: Early crucible smelting of copper on the Iranian plateau.
notes: Dating vs Belovode close; Anatolian claims too.

name: gold working
making_significance: First known large hoard of worked gold, from a cemetery at Varna.

name: lost-wax casting
date_note: Mehrgarh wheel-shaped amulet c. 4500–3600 BCE; Nahal Mishmar hoard c. 3700 BCE
making_significance: First known lost-wax castings.
notes: Thoury et al. 2016.

name: tin bronze
date_note: c. 4650 BCE (Pločnik, Serbia); regular tin bronze c. 3000 BCE
making_significance: First known tin-bronze object.
notes: Radivojević et al. 2013; single find.

name: metallurgy (Andes)
making_significance: Independent start of metallurgy in the Andes with hammered gold foil.
notes: Aldenderfer et al. 2008.

name: native copper (Great Lakes)
making_significance: Among the world's earliest metal working: Great Lakes peoples hammered native copper into tools.
notes: Pompeani et al. 2021 dating.

name: metallurgy (West Mexico)
making_significance: Metallurgy in West Mexico, probably introduced by sea from South America.
notes: Hosler's maritime-contact thesis.

name: platinum working
making_significance: First known working of platinum, sintered with gold by La Tolita-Tumaco metalworkers.

name: meteoric iron
making_significance: First known iron objects, hammered from meteorites.

name: iron smelting (Anatolia)
date_note: Early smelted iron c. 2000 BCE (Kaman-Kalehöyük); common after c. 1200 BCE
making_significance: First known smelted iron.
notes: "Hittite monopoly" story is outdated.

name: iron smelting (sub-Saharan Africa)
date_note: Nok furnaces (incl. Taruga) mostly mid-1st millennium BCE; Taruga dates spread c. 800 BCE–50 CE; Great Lakes c. 1st millennium BCE
making_significance: Early iron smelting in West and East Africa, likely independent.
notes: Independence from North Africa debated; dates vary by site.

name: iron smelting (early African claims)
date_note: Lejja c. 2000 BCE and Termit c. 1500 BCE claimed
making_significance: Contested claims for much earlier iron smelting in Nigeria and Niger.
notes: Radiocarbon on charcoal contested; teach as disputed.

name: cast iron
making_significance: First known cast iron, poured into moulds.
notes: Some date it to the 8th century BCE.

name: crucible steel
date_note: c. 3rd century BCE (South India, Sri Lanka)
making_significance: Early high-carbon crucible steel, later forged into "Damascus" blades.
notes: Dates and sites debated.

name: zinc distillation
date_note: earliest zinc-smelting ash at Zawar dated 840±110 CE; industrial scale from the 11th–12th c.
making_significance: First known industrial zinc production by distillation.
notes: Checked (Craddock et al.; Gurjar et al. 2001): zinc mining at Zawar from c. 5th c. BCE, metallic zinc by distillation from c. 9th c. CE.

name: string
making_significance: First known twisted cord, made by Neanderthals.
notes: Hardy et al. 2020.

name: spun fibre
making_significance: Among the earliest spun and dyed plant fibres.
notes: Kvavadze et al. 2009; fibres could be natural.

name: woven textile impressions
making_significance: First known evidence of woven textiles, as impressions in fired clay.
notes: Adovasio, Soffer and colleagues.

name: twined textiles (Americas)
making_significance: First known textiles of the Americas.
notes: Jolie et al. 2011.

name: linen textiles
making_significance: Early surviving linen textiles, made mostly without a loom.

name: loom depiction
date_note: Naqada I–IIB bowl from Badari tomb 3802 (Petrie Museum UC9547), c. 3900–3500 BCE; Badari is the find-place, not the Badarian period
making_significance: Earliest known image of a loom: probably a horizontal ground loom, painted on a bowl from Badari in Egypt.
notes: Checked: earlier "c. 4400 BCE" was wrong (Badarian date applied to a Naqada bowl). Reading as a loom is probable, not certain.

name: silk
date_note: Silk fabric c. 3500 BCE (Qingtai); Jiahu silk proteins c. 6500 BCE (contested)
making_significance: First known silk textiles.
notes: Jiahu evidence (Gong et al. 2016) debated (low).

name: wild silk (Indus)
making_significance: Independent use of wild silk in the Indus civilization.
notes: Good et al. 2009.

name: cotton (South Asia)
making_significance: First known cotton, preserved in a copper bead.
notes: Moulhérat et al. 2002.

name: cotton (Americas)
making_significance: Independent domestication and weaving of cotton in South America.

name: indigo dyeing
making_significance: First known indigo-dyed textiles, from Peru.
notes: Splitstoser et al. 2016; beats Egyptian evidence by about 1,500 years.

name: pile carpet
making_significance: Oldest surviving knotted-pile carpet, preserved in ice in a Pazyryk burial.

name: trousers
making_significance: Oldest known trousers, from a horseman's grave in the Tarim Basin.
notes: Beck et al. 2014.

name: leather shoe
making_significance: Oldest known leather shoe, from a cave in Armenia.
notes: Pinhasi et al. 2010.

name: drawloom
making_significance: First known pattern loom models, buried in a tomb at Chengdu.
notes: Whether they are drawlooms is debated.

name: Jacquard loom
making_significance: First loom mechanism controlled by punched cards.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)
notes: Builds on Bouchon (1725) and Vaucanson (1745).

name: sea crossing
making_significance: First known open-sea voyages, needed to reach Australia and New Guinea.
notes: Madjedbebe 65,000 BP dating debated.

name: dugout canoe
making_significance: Oldest known boat.

name: dugout canoe (Africa)
making_significance: Oldest known boat in Africa, found in northeast Nigeria.
notes: Dating by radiocarbon; debated.

name: seagoing reed boat
making_significance: First known remains of seagoing boats, bitumen-coated reed, with a painted image of a sail.
notes: Carter 2006; sail image interpretation debated.

name: sail
date_note: Naqada-period Egypt c. 3300 BCE; Ubaid disc c. 5000 BCE claimed
making_significance: First known sails, shown in Egyptian and Gulf images.
notes: Earliest image contested.

name: plank-built ship
date_note: Abydos c. 3000 BCE; Khufu ship c. 2500 BCE
making_significance: First known plank-built ships.

name: outrigger canoe
making_significance: The outrigger stabilised small hulls for ocean voyaging across the Indo-Pacific.
notes: No early physical remains; inferred from linguistics and spread.

name: stick chart
making_significance: First recorded ocean-swell charts, made in the Marshall Islands.
notes: No earlier date is known; the practice is older than its recording.

name: wheel
date_note: c. 3500–3300 BCE (Bronocice pot; Ljubljana Marshes wheel c. 3150 BCE)
making_significance: First known wheels on vehicles, appearing nearly at once from Europe to Mesopotamia.
notes: Place of origin unknown.

name: wheel (Mesoamerica)
making_significance: The wheel was known in Mesoamerica on toys and figurines but not used for transport.
notes: Teaches that "invented" does not mean "used".

name: potter's wheel
date_note: Ubaid c. 4500 BCE (slow wheel); fast wheel later
making_significance: First known turning device for pottery.

name: spoked-wheel chariot
making_significance: First known spoked-wheel chariots, buried in Sintashta graves.

name: skis
making_significance: Oldest known ski fragment, from northern Russia.

name: dog sled
making_significance: First known sled dogs, bred for hauling.
notes: Sinding et al. 2020.

name: stirrup
making_significance: First known stirrups.
notes: Indian toe stirrups (2nd century BCE) claimed; White's "stirrup thesis" (F1.3).

name: saddle
making_significance: Among the earliest surviving saddles.

name: magnetic compass
making_significance: First known magnetised-needle compass and its use at sea.
notes: Han "south-pointing spoon" disputed; Europe c. 1190 (Neckam).

name: wheelbarrow
making_significance: First known wheelbarrows.
notes: Greek evidence possibly earlier.

name: bicycle
making_significance: First known human-powered two-wheelers.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)

name: monumental enclosures
making_significance: First known monumental stone architecture, built by hunter-gatherers.
notes: Upends "farming first, monuments later"; purpose debated.

name: proto-town
making_significance: Large early settlement of mud-brick houses entered through the roof.
notes: Whether a "town" is debated.

name: city (Mesopotamia)
making_significance: First known city at scale.
notes: Tell Brak also early.

name: city (Americas)
making_significance: First known city of the Americas, with platform mounds and plazas.

name: city (Africa, heterarchical)
making_significance: An early West African city without palaces or a ruling centre.
notes: McIntosh; challenges ideas of what makes a city.

name: mega-settlements
making_significance: Settlements of thousands of houses in Ukraine, possibly the largest of their time.
notes: Urban status debated.

name: earthen mounds (North America)
making_significance: First known monumental earthworks of the Americas, built by foragers.

name: true arch and vault
date_note: Mud-brick arches and vaults c. 3rd millennium BCE (approximate)
making_significance: Early true arches and vaults in mud brick.
notes: Earliest example not agreed.

name: concrete (Roman)
making_significance: Hydraulic lime and volcanic-ash concrete that let Romans build vaults and harbours.
notes: Earlier lime plasters (Neolithic Levant) and Nabataean hydraulic mortars.

name: large concrete dome
making_significance: The largest unreinforced concrete dome, still standing.
notes: Earlier corbelled domes (Mycenaean tholoi) differ in technique.

name: qanat and falaj
date_note: Hili 15 and Bida Bint Saud (UAE) aflaj with Iron Age II pottery, c. 1000–600 BCE; Iranian qanats argued to be as early or earlier; no secure absolute dates on either side
making_significance: First known underground channels that carry groundwater by gravity; priority contested between Iran and southeast Arabia.
notes: Aflaj at Hili/Al Ain claimed c. 1000 BCE; Iranian claims similar.

name: windmill
making_significance: First known windmills, with vertical axles, in Sistan.
notes: European post mills c. 1180s are separate.

name: stone tools
date_note: Lomekwi 3 c. 3.3 million years (contested); Oldowan c. 2.6 million years (Gona)
making_significance: First known stone tools.
notes: Lomekwi dating and tool status debated.

name: hand axe
making_significance: First known shaped bifacial tools.

name: wooden spear
making_significance: Oldest known complete wooden hunting weapons.
notes: Redated from c. 400,000 BP.

name: paint workshop
making_significance: First known paint-making kit: ochre mixed in abalone shells.
notes: Henshilwood et al. 2011.

name: shell beads
date_note: c. 142,000–150,000 BP (Bizmoune, Morocco); Blombos c. 75,000 BP
making_significance: First known personal ornaments.
notes: Sehasseh et al. 2021.

name: abstract engraving
date_note: c. 75,000 BP; Trinil shell c. 500,000 BP (Homo erectus, contested)
making_significance: Early deliberate geometric marks.

name: figurative painting
date_note: Leang Karampuang c. 51,200 BP (2024); Leang Tedongnge c. 45,500 BP
making_significance: First known figurative and narrative paintings, in Sulawesi, older than European cave art.
notes: Overturned the Europe-first view (F1.3).

name: musical instrument
making_significance: First known musical instruments.
notes: Divje Babe "Neanderthal flute" contested.

name: playable flute (East Asia)
making_significance: Oldest known playable instruments, crane-bone flutes from Jiahu.

name: edge-ground axe
making_significance: First known ground-edge axes, from northern Australia.
notes: Hiscock et al. 2016.

name: seed grinding
date_note: Madjedbebe Phase 2 (68.7–50.4 ka): seed-grinding use-wear on two grindstones (Hayes et al. 2022), within a debated 65 ka chronology; Cuddie Springs c. 30,000 BP
making_significance: Among the earliest seed-grinding tools.
notes: Madjedbebe dating debated.

name: boomerang
date_note: Wyrie Swamp c. 10,000 BP; Obłazowa Cave ivory object older
making_significance: First known boomerangs.
notes: Obłazowa object dating and function debated.

name: fishhook
making_significance: First known fishhooks, of shell.

name: harpoon
making_significance: First known barbed bone points, for fishing.
notes: Dating debated.

name: bow and arrow
date_note: c. 64,000 BP (Sibudu); Fa-Hien Lena (Sri Lanka) c. 48,000 BP
making_significance: First known arrowheads.
notes: Identification as arrows debated.

name: eyed needle
date_note: Strashnaya Cave c. 44–49 ka; Denisova Cave needle claimed >50 ka on one radiocarbon date, but most of layer 11 dates 25–20 ka (Jacobs et al. 2025)
making_significance: Among the earliest known eyed needles, from Siberian caves.
notes: Dating debated.

name: mirror
making_significance: First known mirrors.

name: dentistry
making_significance: First known dental drilling on living people.
notes: Coppa et al. 2006.

name: surgical amputation
making_significance: First known surgical amputation with survival.
notes: Maloney et al. 2022; human remains—no images.

name: artificial mummification
making_significance: First known artificial mummification, older than Egypt's.
notes: Human remains: no images; World Heritage 2021.

name: tattooing
date_note: Gebelein Man c. 3350 BCE (figurative); Ötzi c. 3250 BCE
making_significance: First known tattoos on preserved bodies.
notes: Human remains: no images.

name: functional prosthesis
making_significance: Earliest known functional prosthesis, a wooden toe.
notes: Finch et al. tested wearability.

name: variolation
date_note: China 16th century (texts); Ottoman, Indian and West African practice
making_significance: Early inoculation against smallpox, known from Onesimus to Boston (1721).
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Wellcome Collection (CC BY / PD)
notes: Onesimus, an enslaved African, informed Cotton Mather.

name: vaccination
making_significance: First vaccination using cowpox.
free_sources: Wellcome Collection (CC BY / PD); Wikimedia Commons
notes: Benjamin Jesty earlier (1774).

name: eyeglasses
making_significance: First known eyeglasses.
free_sources: Wellcome Collection (CC BY / PD); Wikimedia Commons
notes: Giordano da Pisa sermon 1306.

name: braille
making_significance: First tactile writing system for blind readers by Louis Braille.
notes: Built on Barbier's night writing.

name: gunpowder
date_note: Formulae in Wujing Zongyao 1044; earlier 9th-century texts
making_significance: First known gunpowder formulae.

name: firearm
making_significance: Oldest known dated metal gun.
notes: Fire lances earlier.

name: crossbow
making_significance: First known crossbow triggers.

name: paper money
making_significance: First state-issued paper money.

name: coinage (Lydia)
making_significance: First known coins.
notes: A recurrence with China and India.

name: coinage (China)
making_significance: Independent invention of metal currency cast in tool shapes.

name: coinage (India)
making_significance: Independent invention of coins in South Asia.

name: cylinder seal
making_significance: First known cylinder seals.

name: standard weights
making_significance: Early standardised weight system across a region.

name: steam engine
making_significance: First practical steam engine, used to pump mines.
free_sources: Wikimedia Commons; Science Museum Group collection (link out; data CC0)
